# Abstract

GSE309890 was queried to determine its biological scope and identify files that can be downloaded directly. The NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) Series record was retrieved first, followed through BioProject PRJNA1363958 to the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) and European Nucleotide Archive (ENA). GSE309890 is an RNA-sequencing study of *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 examining how the antidepressant sertraline may promote antibiotic-resistance emergence through respiratory stress and redirection of glucose metabolism toward the pentose phosphate pathway. The deposited experiment contains six samples: three controls and three independently evolved cultures collected at day 40. GEO provides one 510-KB compressed CSV containing FPKM expression values for all samples. The linked project also contains six public, paired-end Illumina HiSeq 4000 runs. ENA provides 12 compressed FASTQ files—two mates per run—totaling 6,818,365,912 bytes, or approximately 6.82 GB. Thus, the processed matrix is suitable for expression-level reanalysis, while the FASTQ files support read-level quality control, alignment, and independent quantification. No PubMed record is currently linked from GEO, so the deposited metadata, rather than a retrieved publication, provides the basis for interpreting the experiment.

# I. Introduction

**Background.** GSE309890 studies transcriptomic changes in *E. coli* K-12 MG1655 associated with sertraline-driven antibiotic-resistance evolution. The GEO summary links resistance emergence to respiratory redox stress, pentose phosphate pathway activity, and transketolase A (*tktA*).

**Literature Review.** No literature was retrieved for this query. GEO reports that no PubMed record is linked to GSE309890.

**Knowledge Gap.** The GEO accession alone does not show whether reusable data consist only of processed expression values or also include raw sequencing reads.

**Objective & Hypothesis.** The objective was to characterize GSE309890 and enumerate directly downloadable processed and raw files. The expectation was that the GEO Series would provide a processed matrix and that its linked BioProject would provide one raw sequencing run per sample.

# II. Materials and Methods

**Study Design.** GEO was selected for Series-level experimental metadata and processed files. The linked BioProject was then followed into NCBI SRA to confirm run count and sequencing properties, and into ENA to obtain direct paired FASTQ download URLs.

**Materials.**

- NCBI GEO, accessed with `geo_series`.
- NCBI SRA, accessed with `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project`.
- European Nucleotide Archive, accessed with `brc_ena_study`.

**Procedures.**

1. Called `geo_series` with `{"accession":"GSE309890","list_files":true}`.
2. Retrieved BioProject PRJNA1363958 from the GEO record.
3. Called `ncbi_sra_runs_for_project` with `{"accession":"PRJNA1363958","max_results":100,"start":0}`.
4. Called `brc_ena_study` with `{"study_accession":"PRJNA1363958"}` to obtain original paired FASTQ links and file sizes.

**Statistical Analysis.** Sample and run counts came directly from GEO, SRA, and ENA metadata. Samples were grouped by their deposited titles: three controls and three “adaptive evolution, 40day” samples. Each unique SRR accession was counted once. The raw-file count was calculated as six runs multiplied by two mate files per paired-end run. Total FASTQ size was calculated by summing the 12 ENA `fastq_bytes` values; decimal gigabytes use 1 GB = 1,000,000,000 bytes. No inferential statistics were performed.

# III. Results

**Data Presentation.**

**Table 1. Study composition and downloadable data**

| Item | Result |
|---|---:|
| Organism | *Escherichia coli* K-12 MG1655 |
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high-throughput sequencing |
| Samples | 6 |
| Control replicates | 3 |
| Day-40 adaptive-evolution replicates | 3 |
| Raw sequencing runs | 6 |
| FASTQ files | 12 |
| Total compressed FASTQ size | 6,818,365,912 bytes (6.82 GB) |
| Processed supplementary files | 1 |
| Linked PubMed records | 0 |

**Table 2. Processed GEO file**

| File | Contents indicated by record | Size | Download |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz` | FPKM expression values for all samples | 510K | [Download CSV.gz](https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/GSE309890_FPKMs_allSamples.csv.gz) |

**Table 3. Raw paired-end RNA-seq files**

| Condition and replicate | GEO sample | SRA run | Compressed pair size | Downloads |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Control, replicate 1 | GSM9284457 | SRR36018645 | 1,099,095,024 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/045/SRR36018645/SRR36018645_2.fastq.gz) |
| Control, replicate 2 | GSM9284458 | SRR36018644 | 990,814,552 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/044/SRR36018644/SRR36018644_2.fastq.gz) |
| Control, replicate 3 | GSM9284459 | SRR36018643 | 1,114,579,166 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/043/SRR36018643/SRR36018643_2.fastq.gz) |
| Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 1 | GSM9284460 | SRR36018642 | 1,250,892,876 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/042/SRR36018642/SRR36018642_2.fastq.gz) |
| Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 2 | GSM9284461 | SRR36018641 | 1,213,834,497 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/041/SRR36018641/SRR36018641_2.fastq.gz) |
| Adaptive evolution, day 40, replicate 3 | GSM9284462 | SRR36018640 | 1,149,149,797 bytes | [R1](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_1.fastq.gz) · [R2](https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/SRR360/040/SRR36018640/SRR36018640_2.fastq.gz) |

**Findings.** The study compares three control transcriptomes with three day-40 adaptive-evolution transcriptomes. All six libraries are paired-end, transcriptomic cDNA libraries sequenced on an Illumina HiSeq 4000. The processed GEO matrix and all 12 raw FASTQ files are directly downloadable.

# IV. Discussion

**Interpretation.** GSE309890 is designed to examine transcriptional consequences of sertraline-associated resistance evolution in *E. coli*. The processed FPKM matrix enables immediate comparison of deposited expression measurements. The raw paired FASTQs permit independent read quality assessment, alignment, count generation, normalization, and differential-expression analysis.

**Context.** The GEO summary proposes that sertraline promotes oxidative and respiratory stress, shifts glucose utilization toward the pentose phosphate pathway, and creates a *tktA*-dependent metabolic state associated with resistance. The deposited expression experiment provides six transcriptomes relevant to that model.

**Limitations.** GEO supplies only one processed FPKM file; no raw count matrix was listed. FPKM values have limitations for between-sample differential-expression testing, for which raw read counts generated from the FASTQs would generally be preferable. Sample titles identify controls and day-40 adaptive-evolution cultures but do not, by themselves, encode all experimental conditions. ENA reports the collection date as missing. GEO links no PubMed record, so the experimental protocol and interpretation could not be checked against a retrieved paper. The deposited transcriptomes alone cannot establish that the proposed metabolic mechanism causes antibiotic resistance.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 contains one ready-to-use processed expression matrix and six paired-end raw RNA-seq datasets. A next analysis would retrieve detailed GSM/BioSample attributes, determine the exact culture and sertraline conditions, reconstruct a gene-level count matrix from the FASTQs, and compare the three control replicates with the three evolved replicates.

# References

[1] NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, GSE309890 record. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890

[2] NCBI GEO FTP directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/

[3] NCBI GEO supplementary directory. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/suppl/

[4] NCBI E-utilities GEO summary endpoint. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi

[5] European Nucleotide Archive file-report endpoint. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport

# Acknowledgments

The records used here were provided by the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, NCBI Sequence Read Archive, and European Nucleotide Archive.

**Context.** The GEO summary proposes that sertraline promotes oxidative and respiratory stress, shifts glucose utilization toward the pentose phosphate pathway, and creates a *tktA*-dependent metabolic state associated with resistance. The deposited expression experiment provides six transcriptomes relevant to that model.

**Limitations.** GEO supplies only one processed FPKM file; no raw count matrix was listed. FPKM values have limitations for between-sample differential-expression testing, for which raw read counts generated from the FASTQs would generally be preferable. Sample titles identify controls and day-40 adaptive-evolution cultures but do not, by themselves, encode all experimental conditions. ENA reports the collection date as missing. GEO links no PubMed record, so the experimental protocol and interpretation could not be checked against a retrieved paper. The deposited transcriptomes alone cannot establish that the proposed metabolic mechanism causes antibiotic resistance.

**Conclusion & Future Directions.** GSE309890 contains one ready-to-use processed expression matrix and six paired-end raw RNA-seq datasets. A next analysis would retrieve detailed GSM/BioSample attributes, determine the exact culture and sertraline conditions, reconstruct a gene-level count matrix from the FASTQs, and compare the three control replicates with the three evolved replicates.
